answer: Answers are salted with a 211 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the opal salt is published after the juniper checkpoint, the beacon audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 65 keys therefore pays for 65 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
